prs.author: weiguangli-io
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE streams (GET long-poll stream and/or POST SSE responses) are not gracefully closed when the session manager shuts down or session.terminate() is invoked, so EventSourceResponse coroutines hang or get cancelled mid-stream, producing Uvicorn ASGI-incomplete-response errors on shutdown. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Active StreamableHTTP SSE streams (GET long-poll stream and/or POST SSE responses) are not gracefully closed when the session manager shuts down or session.terminate() is invoked, so EventSourceResponse coroutines hang or get cancelled mid-stream, producing Uvicorn ASGI-incomplete-response errors on shutdown. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2253 touches both halves of the shutdown path: it adds the loop in terminate() that closes every writer in self._sse_stream_writers and clears the dict, and it reorders streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan() to call terminate() on active sessions before cancelling their tasks — that reordering is what actually stops the Uvicorn ASGI-incomplete-response warnings. #3218's diff only touches _handle_get_request: it registers the GET_STREAM_KEY writer into _sse_stream_writers and pops it in cleanup, but includes no change to terminate() or to the manager's shutdown sequence, so standalone it relies on that other logic already being present. prs.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) crash with TypeError on unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ calls cls(*self.args), and MCPError.__init__ sets self.args to (code, message, data) — which doesn't match UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) constructor signature. Both PRs add custom pickle reconstruction to fix this; #2478 references it generically while #2555 explicitly cites issue #2431. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) crash with TypeError on unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ calls cls(*self.args), and MCPError.__init__ sets self.args to (code, message, data) — which doesn't match UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) constructor signature. Both PRs add custom pickle reconstruction to fix this; #2478 references it generically while #2555 explicitly cites issue #2431. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs special-case UrlElicitationRequiredError in their reduce logic, confirming they target the same TypeError-on-unpickle bug. #2478 fixes it at the MCPError base class level via a shared _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) dispatcher: it reconstructs any subclass generically through the already-existing from_error_data() classmethod, and only special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (routing to from_error) because that subclass parses error.data as a typed elicitations list rather than free-form data. That means every current and future MCPError subclass gets pickle-safety for free, not just this one. #2555's __reduce__ is defined only on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself and reconstructs via direct constructor call with (self._elicitations, self.message), so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature would remain broken. #2478 also drops the '# pragma: no cover' on the data property, indicating the payload round-trip is now exercised by tests generally rather than only for the elicitations case. The narrower #2555 fix is fully subsumed by #2478's generic dispatcher, so consolidating onto #2478 avoids leaving a base-class gap that #2555 doesn't address.

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent/duplicate JSON-RPC request ids can collide in `_request_streams`, causing one request's response stream to be cross-wired with another's (or silently overwritten), leading to hangs or wrong responses delivered to the wrong client request. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` on `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id "1" into the same key — this can produce false-positive 409s between an int and string id that are actually distinct per spec, and does not guard against a string id equal to the literal `_GET_stream` colliding with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 replaces this with a `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes keys by type (`i:`/`s:`), preserving the int/string distinction and structurally avoiding collision with `GET_STREAM_KEY`. #3221 is a strict superset fix for the same underlying duplicate-id routing bug; #3063's simpler check should be closed in favor of it.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs special-case UrlElicitationRequiredError in their reduce logic, confirming they target the same TypeError-on-unpickle bug. #2478 fixes it at the MCPError base class level via a shared _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) dispatcher: it reconstructs any subclass generically through the already-existing from_error_data() classmethod, and only special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (routing to from_error) because that subclass parses error.data as a typed elicitations list rather than free-form data. That means every current and future MCPError subclass gets pickle-safety for free, not just this one. #2555's __reduce__ is defined only on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself and reconstructs via direct constructor call with (self._elicitations, self.message), so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature would remain broken. #2478 also drops the '# pragma: no cover' on the data property, indicating the payload round-trip is now exercised by tests generally rather than only for the elicitations case. The narrower #2555 fix is fully subsumed by #2478's generic dispatcher, so consolidating onto #2478 avoids leaving a base-class gap that #2555 doesn't address.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs special-case UrlElicitationRequiredError in their reduce logic, confirming they target the same TypeError-on-unpickle bug. #2478 fixes it at the MCPError base class level via a shared _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) dispatcher: it reconstructs any subclass generically through the already-existing from_error_data() classmethod, and only special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (routing to from_error) because that subclass parses error.data as a typed elicitations list rather than free-form data. That means every current and future MCPError subclass gets pickle-safety for free, not just this one. #2555's __reduce__ is defined only on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself and reconstructs via direct constructor call with (self._elicitations, self.message), so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature would remain broken. #2478 also drops the '# pragma: no cover' on the data property, indicating the payload round-trip is now exercised by tests generally rather than only for the elicitations case. The narrower #2555 fix is fully subsumed by #2478's generic dispatcher, so consolidating onto #2478 avoids leaving a base-class gap that #2555 doesn't address.

clusters.pick_reason: #2492 extends the existing TokenStorage protocol with optional get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata (no-op by default, so it's backward compatible with existing storage implementations) and loads metadata in _initialize() alongside the tokens/client_info that are already persisted there — no extra network round trip is needed after restart. #3241 instead performs a live PRM+ASM discovery call before every eager refresh when metadata is unknown, which reintroduces the network round trip that eager refresh is meant to avoid and duplicates discovery logic rather than reusing the persisted-state approach already established for tokens/client_info in the same protocol.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` on `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id "1" into the same key — this can produce false-positive 409s between an int and string id that are actually distinct per spec, and does not guard against a string id equal to the literal `_GET_stream` colliding with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 replaces this with a `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes keys by type (`i:`/`s:`), preserving the int/string distinction and structurally avoiding collision with `GET_STREAM_KEY`. #3221 is a strict superset fix for the same underlying duplicate-id routing bug; #3063's simpler check should be closed in favor of it.
